title: What to see and do at Social Good Summit 2026’s XChange
summary: At this year’s Social Good Summit, participants can explore interactive booths and activities from organizations working on human rights, local governance, digital safety, and other social issues

blocks.text: At this year’s Social Good Summit, participants can explore interactive booths and activities from organizations working on human rights, local governance, digital safety, and other social issues
MANILA, Philippines – What makes us human in an age of artificial intelligence (AI)?
At the Social Good Summit 2026, XChange offers participants a chance to explore this question and other social issues featuring interactive games, exhibits, and activities from partner organizations.
XChange is an interactive exhibition space where organizations, advocacy groups, and brands showcase their work, campaigns, and initiatives and engage with summit participants.
Here are some of the activities from this year’s XChange exhibitors:

90 Degrees North, a media production company specializing in broadcast and virtual production, will let visitors experience how a modern newsroom operates. Its booth will feature a broadcast setup with real-time graphics, virtual production, broadcast cameras, professional lighting, and a teleprompter.

DAKILA, a nonprofit organization that uses arts and culture to promote human rights and social change, invites visitors to explore what makes a hero human in an age of artificial intelligence through a timed challenge. Participants must assemble a face using detachable eyes, ears, nose, and mouth without directly seeing where they place the pieces.
Visitors can compete head-to-head or try the solo challenge. The winner of the head-to-head round receives a prize from DAKILA.

The Initiatives for Dialogue and Empowerment through Alternative Legal Services (IDEALS), a nonprofit organization that provides legal services and promotes access to justice for marginalized communities, will showcase visual exhibits from S’bang Ka Mindanao and ALPAS-KP, which highlight IDEALS’ work with Marawi’s displaced communities and victim-survivors of the war on drugs.
Visitors can also join mini-trivia games and play quick rounds of Sitio Norain and Project Masikap.
Learn more about local governance, government programs, and initiatives through activities from the two Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) booths.

At the DILG Calabarzon booth, take on DILG Unboxed, a quick trivia challenge that will feature questions about the department and its work. Participants who answer correctly can win small prizes and tokens.

At the DILG Laguna booth, explore local governance initiatives and best practices through information materials and videos from the Local Governance Resource Center (LGRC) Laguna. Visitors can also play LGRC Scratch and Win for a chance to win prizes by matching three identical LGRC partner logos.

Dapat Isa Lang People’s Initiative, a campaign calling for the passage of an anti-dynasty law, will also be present for a live petition signing. Facilitators will guide visitors through the signing process and answer questions from those interested in supporting the initiative.

JenCanCraft creates advocacy-related products, including its Stop Bullying 3D-printed whistles. Visitors can write an anti-bullying pledge, an encouraging message, or a commitment to act against harassment on the booth’s community pledge wall.
Visitors can also customize tote bags at the on-site pressing station by choosing words, initials, or advocacy designs.

The Ateneo Human Rights Center, a university-based institution that promotes and protects human rights through education, research, and legal advocacy, will offer information materials, interactive activities, and stickers at its booth.
Visitors can learn more about the center’s work on access to justice and the promotion and protection of human rights.

The Foundation for Media Alternatives, a nonprofit organization advocating for digital rights and the use of information and communications technologies for social development, will showcase publications, comics, coloring books, and other resources on collective care.
Visitors can take home free publications and stickers, and join conversations about technology-facilitated gender-based violence, including ways to respond to it.
Visit Rappler’s booths to explore its community platform, learning resources, membership offerings, and merchandise.

At the Muni booth, discover Rappler’s community platform and test your knowledge through a Match the Logo game. At the joint RappLearn and Rappler+, visitors can learn about Rappler’s learning platform and membership offerings.

You can also visit the Rappler Merchandise booth to purchase Rappler CEO and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Maria Ressa’s latest book, The Fight Back: A Citizen’s Guide to Standing Up to Dictators. The first 30 buyers will get the chance to have their copies signed by Ressa.
Other exhibitors at XChange include GCash, Linya-Linya, and Ogis which will also have booths at the summit.
All attendees will receive an Event Passport during registration. The passport has two tracks: one for the masterclasses and another for the XChange booths.
For the XChange track, participants must visit all participating booths, take part in their activities, and collect a mark from each booth, for a chance to win a prize.

Once completed, participants must take a selfie with the marked passport and post it in the Everyday Tech chat room, along with a short takeaway from the summit. Entries must be submitted by 4:30 pm to qualify for the XChange raffle.

A separate raffle is open to attendees who complete all the masterclasses assigned to them, including the Living in Water: A 360° Virtual Reality Immersion into the Climate Crisis screening. To qualify, participants must also post a photo of their completed passport and a takeaway on the Everyday Tech chat room by 5 pm.
Three winners will be drawn for each raffle. Winners will be announced at 5:30 pm and can claim their prizes at the Help Desk.
Attendees may join either or both raffles, depending on the activities they complete.
For more information about the Social Good Summit 2026, visit rplr.co/AboutSGS2026. – Rappler.com
